channel.title: Farmer's Weekly SA - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Farmer's Weekly SA (farmersweekly.co.za)

item.title: How school nutrition programmes can boost nutrition and drive transformation
item.description: The National School Nutrition Programme feeds more than nine million school children every day and remains one of South Africa’s most meaningful interventions for supporting learning and reducing hunger. But with strategic partnerships, the programme could do far more, strengthening childhood nutrition while helping to drive transformation across the agriculture sector.

item.title: State of the Nation Address met with scepticism over implementation
item.description: The State of the Nation Address (SONA) 2026, delivered by President Cyril Ramaphosa on Thursday evening in Cape Town, highlighted progress made in growing the economy and reducing unemployment, but numerous challenges still inhibit the country from achieving real change.

item.title: Power and intelligence working together
item.description: The new John Deere S7 Combine offers innovative improvements that help farmers get more out of every hour in the field.

item.title: Does the FMD Industry Coordination Council actually have a voice?
item.description: Many in the agriculture sector welcomed Agriculture Minister John Steenhuisen’s 21 January announcement of the formation of a foot-and-mouth disease (FMD) Industry Coordination Council. The body enables farmer organisations to join a three-way partnership aimed at strengthening and supporting the national FMD response.

item.title: Bitter end looms for Tongaat Hulett as rescue efforts collapse
item.description: The long-running business rescue of Tongaat Hulett Limited has reached a decisive turning point, with joint business rescue practitioners (BRPs) applying to the KwaZulu-Natal Division of the High Court to discontinue rescue proceedings and place the 134-year-old sugar producer into provisional liquidation.

item.title: Farmers urged to co-operate with FMD inspections
item.description: Following a recent case of a farmer refusing state veterinarians access to his property, officials have emphasised farmers’ legal duties in foot-and-mouth disease (FMD) control zones and the need to co-operate with inspections.

item.title: Tata in for a rough ride in re-establishing itself in SA with Harrier
item.description: Indian carmaker Tata re-entered the local passenger car market last year with a line-up headed by the brand’s only diesel offering, the Harrier. The Citizen’s Charl Bosch put the SUV to the test.

item.title: National FMD disaster: coordination breakthrough or centralisation risk?
item.description: South Africa’s escalating foot-and-mouth disease (FMD) outbreak has now been formally classified as a national disaster under Section 23 of the Disaster Management Act (No. 57 of 2002).

item.title: MEC Vuyiswa Ramokgopa oulines Gauteng’s FMD containment plan
item.description: Foot-and-mouth disease is putting farmers under extreme pressure.

item.title: How women are transforming coffee production in Kenya
item.description: A group of Kenyan smallholder women farmers are transforming the country’s high-value coffee sector by pooling their resources.
